description: Playwright Test Builder page — where users create, edit, and manage Playwright browser automation tests that serve as verification steps in workflows

groups.name: Page Purpose
groups.description: The Playwright Test Builder enables users to create browser automation tests using Playwright. These tests serve as powerful verification steps in workflows, allowing AI-driven automation to validate that web applications behave correctly after changes. Users write TypeScript/JavaScript test code, run tests, and view results including failure screenshots.

assertions.description: Users can create new Playwright tests by writing TypeScript test code that verifies web application behavior
Users can use saved Playwright tests as verification steps in workflows, giving the AI concrete pass/fail signals about application state
Users can browse all saved Playwright tests in a searchable list and select any test for editing, running, or review

groups.name: Test Authoring Goals
groups.description: Users need a productive test authoring experience with code editing, syntax highlighting, and quick access to common Playwright patterns. The editor should make it easy to write assertions that verify page content, element state, and user interaction outcomes.

assertions.description: Users can write and edit Playwright test code in a code editor with syntax highlighting for TypeScript/JavaScript
Users can give each test a descriptive name that identifies what it verifies when browsing the test library
Users can save test code to the library for reuse across multiple workflows

groups.name: Test Execution Goals
groups.description: Users need to run tests directly from the builder to validate their test code works correctly before incorporating tests into workflows. Test execution should provide clear pass/fail results with detailed error messages and failure screenshots.

assertions.description: Users can run a Playwright test directly from the builder and see real-time execution results
Users can see test results with pass/fail status, assertion error messages, and failure screenshots to debug test issues

groups.name: Test Management Goals
groups.description: Users need to manage their test library over time — deleting obsolete tests, updating tests as the application evolves, and organizing tests for easy discovery when building workflows.

assertions.description: Users can delete tests that are no longer relevant, keeping the test library clean and current
Users can search through saved tests to quickly find the right test for their workflow

states.name: Empty Library — No Playwright Tests Exist
states.description: The page loads with no saved Playwright tests. The left panel list is empty. The right panel editor shows a placeholder state inviting the user to create their first test.

transitions.name: Create new test
transitions.description: User initiates creation of a new Playwright test, opening a blank editor with name input and code editor

states.name: Populated — Test List with Editor Idle
states.description: One or more saved Playwright tests exist and are displayed in the left panel list. No test is actively selected for editing. The search box is available for filtering.

transitions.name: Select a test to edit
transitions.description: User clicks a test in the list to load it into the right-panel code editor for viewing or editing

transitions.name: Create new test
transitions.description: User initiates creation of a new Playwright test, clearing the editor to a blank form

transitions.name: Enter search query
transitions.description: User types in the search box to filter the test list by name

states.name: Search Active — Filtering Test List
states.description: A search query has been entered in the search box and the left-panel list is filtered to show only tests matching the query.

transitions.name: Clear search query
transitions.description: User clears the search input to return to the full unfiltered test list

transitions.name: Select a filtered test
transitions.description: User clicks a test from the filtered search results to load it into the editor

states.name: Editing New — Creating a Playwright Test
states.description: The editor is active with a blank test form. Users can enter a test name, write TypeScript test code in the code editor, and save. The Save button is available but Delete is not.

transitions.name: Save new test
transitions.description: User clicks Save to persist the new test to the library, transitioning to editing-existing with the newly saved test loaded

transitions.name: Cancel or select existing test
transitions.description: User clicks a different test in the list, discarding the unsaved new test

states.name: Editing Existing — Modifying a Saved Test
states.description: A saved Playwright test is loaded in the editor. The name field and code editor are populated with the test's current values. Save, Delete, and Run buttons are available.

transitions.name: Save changes
transitions.description: User clicks Save to persist modifications to the existing test

transitions.name: Run test
transitions.description: User clicks the Run button to execute the Playwright test and see results

transitions.name: Delete test
transitions.description: User clicks the Delete button to initiate deletion of the current test

transitions.name: Create new test while editing
transitions.description: User initiates creation of a new test, clearing the editor

transitions.name: Select a different test
transitions.description: User clicks another test in the list to switch to editing that test instead

states.name: Test Running — Executing Playwright Test
states.description: A Playwright test is currently executing. The results area shows execution progress. The editor remains visible with the test code.

transitions.name: Test execution completes
transitions.description: The test finishes executing and results (pass/fail, errors, screenshots) are displayed

states.name: Test Results — Viewing Execution Results
states.description: Test execution has completed and results are displayed showing pass/fail status, assertion error messages, and failure screenshots. The user can edit the test and run again.

transitions.name: Re-run test
transitions.description: User clicks Run again to re-execute the test after making changes

transitions.name: Return to editing
transitions.description: User dismisses results and returns to editing the test code

states.name: Confirm Delete — Deletion Confirmation Dialog
states.description: A confirmation dialog is displayed asking the user to confirm deletion of the selected Playwright test.

transitions.name: Confirm deletion
transitions.description: User confirms the deletion, removing the test from the library and returning to the populated list view

transitions.name: Cancel deletion
transitions.description: User cancels the deletion dialog, returning to the editing state with the test still intact
